headline: Forged in operations.
Engineered for the cloud.
hero.subheadline: AWS Certified Solutions Architect. Built to withstand production traffic. Available now.
hero.footnote: The infrastructure behind this page was provisioned by Terraform and is deployed by a pipeline that holds no AWS keys.

highlights.label: certifications earned
highlights.detail: AWS Solutions Architect Associate, AWS Cloud Practitioner, Linux Essentials, Oracle Cloud Foundations, Google IT Support.

highlights.label: line of Terraform closed an exposed database
highlights.detail: A PostgreSQL database was left open to the internet on purpose. A scripted attack ran against it, real scanners showed up uninvited, and one changed line made it unreachable from outside the VPC.

highlights.label: resources in production, every one in Terraform
highlights.detail: Every bucket, role, function, table, certificate and DNS record lives in a Terraform module. The only clicks were registering the domain and setting up sign in.

highlights.label: long lived keys in CI
highlights.detail: GitHub authenticates to AWS over OpenID Connect. The credentials expire in one hour and are never stored.

projects.title: Enterprise DevSecOps Threat Pipeline
projects.summary: Splunk ingests VPC Flow Logs and CloudTrail, correlation searches mapped to MITRE ATT&CK raise the alert, and a Python Lambda drops a deny rule into the network ACL before a human has read the notification.
projects.detail: I own every piece of AWS infrastructure and all of the Terraform. Kenny Barr owns the Splunk detection engineering and the dashboard work.

metrics.label: hard limit on the containment Lambda

media.alt: Splunk dashboard titled Phase 1 Cryptojacking Detection. An endpoint malware event mapped to MITRE technique T1496 with high severity, an attack timeline broken out by source address, port sweep activity, a threat correlation summary, and a table of the top attacking addresses with their connection counts and targeted ports. One source address is redacted.

projects.title: SecureAccess Audit Dashboard
projects.summary: Parses raw access logs in the browser and scores every session against several risk signals at once, so a reviewer opens the three accounts worth investigating instead of scrolling ten thousand rows.

media.alt: The SecureAccess Audit Dashboard. Four summary tiles reading 44 total events, 17 failed logins, 5 flagged accounts and a highest risk user, a row of filter tabs for failed logins, after hours activity, privilege escalation and suspicious only, and a table of access events with usernames, actions, addresses, departments, status and a threat score per row.

projects.title: AWS Incident Response Honeypot
projects.summary: A PostgreSQL database left open to the internet on purpose, provisioned by Terraform, with flow logs feeding Splunk. A scripted attack ran against it, real internet scanners turned up in the same capture, and one changed line of Terraform made it unreachable from outside the VPC.

media.alt: Splunk panel showing an automation KPI of 77,959 events, beside a statistics table of attacking source addresses with connection counts and the most recent port each one targeted.

projects.title: Serverless Resume Platform
projects.summary: React on a private S3 bucket behind CloudFront, a Python Lambda counting visits in DynamoDB, and two pipelines that deploy it with no stored AWS keys.

projects.title: RHEL LogVault Automation
projects.summary: A Bash script on a RHEL 9 instance that archives the system logs and copies them to an S3 bucket. The instance signs in through an IAM role, so no access key is stored on the box.

items: AWS: EC2, VPC, S3, IAM, Lambda, DynamoDB, CloudFront, Route53, API Gateway, CloudWatch, WAF
Cost aware architecture and on demand capacity choices
Terraform, written as reusable modules with typed variables and validation
Remote state in S3 with DynamoDB locking
Plan review discipline. Nothing reaches production without a readable diff
Splunk SPL, CIM normalization, correlation searches
CloudTrail and VPC Flow Log analysis
Automated containment with Lambda and network ACLs
GitHub Actions with OpenID Connect federation
pytest and moto for AWS unit tests
Least privilege deploy roles, separated for plan and apply
Cache invalidation and immutable asset strategy

experience.summary: Becoming Technologists, a residency where project teams run a simulated consulting firm through design sprints for a real client.
bullets: Solutions analyst and quality engineer on a three person team building a governed answer assistant for a nonprofit client with volunteer run chapters in many countries.

Designed it so rules decide every answer before any AI model runs. It answers only from approved documents that apply to the asker's chapter, shows the source and its effective date, and hands the question to a person when it cannot answer safely.

Wrote the ten question test set the team treats as the contract, five answers and five refusals. The browser prototype passes all ten, and the team has presented it to the client at two sprint reviews.
Built the back end in C#, Blazor and PostgreSQL in Docker, and the team showed it running at the final client presentation.

Runs the guest speaker series for the cohort as its High Tea ambassador, leads a weekly cohort meeting on career paths, and writes a build log of the cycle on dev.to. Week one is in the newsroom below.

experience.summary: Turned the transition into a build log instead of a study plan.
bullets: Provisioned live AWS environments with Terraform, then broke them on purpose and fixed them.
Ran RHEL 9 as a daily administration target rather than a lab exercise.
Shipped a Splunk detection pipeline with automated AWS containment alongside a detection engineer.

experience.summary: Owned a territory of 55 to 60 B2B accounts against quarterly volume targets.
bullets: Ran the entire cycle without a handoff. Prospecting, pricing conversations, merchandising resets, and the follow up that actually closes.
Turned messy field data into forecasts leadership planned around, which is the same job as building a dashboard someone is willing to trust.
Held the line on compliance in a heavily regulated category, where a shortcut is a legal problem, not a style choice.

experience.summary: Eight years of floor operations, scheduling, inventory accuracy and peak season throughput.
bullets: Managed daily operations through eight consecutive peak seasons, where the plan meets reality at nine in the morning and you adjust or you lose the day.
Trained and coached new hires, including the ones other leads passed on.
Owned cash controls and loss prevention, which is where I learned that an audit trail is worth exactly as much as its weakest control.
